## The problem NEAR solves

Crypto is spread across hundreds of blockchains, each with its own assets, apps and rules. Moving money between them usually takes several steps, a bridge, and a fee at each stage. AI has a different problem: a few companies run the most capable models and see everything people send them. As AI agents start to act for people, they will need a way to pay and trade on any chain, and a way to use AI without handing over private data.

NEAR has built a product for each problem. NEAR Intents turns a swap between any two chains into a single step. NEAR AI runs AI models on hardware that keeps prompts private, even from NEAR AI. Both tie back to the NEAR token.

NEAR is still mostly discussed as a base-layer blockchain (an L1), and on L1 numbers alone it looks like a network in decline: L1 transactions fell from {l1_tx_first} a day in {l1_tx_first_month} to {l1_tx_last} in {l1_tx_last_month}. That view misses where the business went.

## Three layers

NEAR now works as three businesses, each built on the one below it.

**NEAR L1, the base chain.** The blockchain itself: accounts, smart contracts and payments, at an average fee of about {l1_fee} a transaction in {m}. Its own traffic has fallen since its two largest consumer apps wound down, but more of what remains is Intents: {c2_share} of L1 transactions in {c2_month} went to the Intents contract, against {c2_share_yago} a year earlier.

**NEAR Intents, cross-chain swaps.** A user says what they have and what they want, and competing market makers (called solvers) fill the order. NEAR settles the result. In {m}, Intents handled {int_vol} of swaps, {int_vol_x} its level a year earlier, and users paid {int_fees} in fees. Swaps started on {int_chains} different chains.

**NEAR AI, private AI.** NEAR AI Cloud runs open AI models inside secure hardware (trusted execution environments, or TEEs), so no one, not even NEAR AI, can read the prompts, and each answer comes with a proof of where it ran. Customers pay per use, or stake NEAR and receive inference credits paid from the staking rewards. It is the newest layer: on OpenRouter it served {ai_first} tokens in the week to {ai_first_week} and {ai_last} in the week to {ai_last_week}, and Brave's AI assistant has run on it since {brave_date}.

**How the layers fit together.** They are designed to feed each other: AI agents need to pay and trade across chains, which is what Intents does, and every Intents swap settles on the L1. Each layer also sends value to the NEAR token, which the next section follows.

## Why the NEAR token has value

The token gains when the network takes NEAR out of circulation, or locks it up, faster than it issues new NEAR. Four changes in the last year moved that balance.

- **Less new supply.** On {infl_date}, NEAR cut its issuance cap from {infl_from} to {infl_to} a year. A second cut, HSP-029, passed on {hsp_passed} and would bring it to {hsp_target} by {hsp_end}.
- **Buybacks.** Since {bb_date}, NEAR's share of Intents fees buys NEAR on the market.
- **A full gas burn.** {gas_txt}
- **Staking for AI.** Since {ai_open}, NEAR AI customers can stake NEAR and receive inference credits. The NEAR stays locked while it is staked.

## Our view

**Long-term bullish.**

NEAR's business has moved beyond the L1. Intents produced {c1_share3} of NEAR's protocol revenue over {c1_last3}, against {c1_share3_yago} a year earlier, and it is taking share in its market rather than just riding it. NEAR AI is the smallest layer, but it is real: paid usage up {ai_x} since its first full week on OpenRouter, a production integration in Brave, and {c5_stake} NEAR staked to pay for it.

The token is only beginning to capture that value, and that is the opportunity. Every mechanism that sends value to the token switched on in the last {mech_months} months. {recent_mechanisms}. If Intents revenue keeps growing at a rate that halves every {base_half_life} years, burns and buybacks offset all new NEAR by {base_cut}.

{scenario_short}

## Appendix

### A. Methods

- **Revenue (C1).** L1 side: NEAR burned by gas, measured from block-to-block changes in total supply (BigQuery), valued at the daily NEAR price (NearBlocks). Intents side: NEAR's net revenue after partner payouts, from revenue.near.org. The net basis compares what the protocol keeps on each side; the gross basis compares all fees users pay. {l1_gross_method}
- **L1 activity (C2).** BigQuery `transactions` table, daily since {l1_start}: transactions, distinct signers (daily active accounts), transactions sent to `intents.near`, the busiest receiving contracts each month, and the two largest consumer apps split out by signer account (KaiChing: `*.kaiching`; HOT: `*.tg` and `hot.tg`). Every query on a block-level table filters on `block_date`; the two balance queries filter on `epoch_date`, the partition column of `ft_balances_daily`.
- **Intents breadth (C3).** NEAR Intents Explorer API, successful swaps. A user is the first sender address of a swap, or its refund address when no sender is given. The top-ten share is the share of a month's volume sent by its ten largest users. Stablecoin shares use the token on each side of the swap.
- **Market share (C4).** DefiLlama daily volumes. Peer set: NEAR Intents, THORChain, Chainflip and Maya Protocol, the venues that swap native assets across chains. Bridge aggregators and total DEX volume are reference series, kept out of the denominator to avoid double counting.
- **NEAR AI (C5).** Tokens per model per day from OpenRouter's NEAR AI provider page. Revenue estimate: NEAR AI's OpenRouter prices for each model, applied with that model's prompt/completion split. Staking from `stake.dao` contract views and archival RPC balances of `nearai.pool.near`; the model catalog from NEAR AI Cloud's public model list.
- **Capture ratio (C6).** Total supply jumps at each epoch boundary by the newly minted NEAR and otherwise only falls, by the NEAR burned; summing those changes gives NEAR issued and burned per day. NEAR captured as Intents revenue comes from revenue.near.org. New AI stake is the month-end change in `nearai.pool.near` stake.
- **Follow the money.** The latest month with complete data for all three layers. NEAR AI's sales there are the OpenRouter estimate above, summed over the month.
- **Protocol parameters.** Issuance cap and the gas rebate to contracts are read from NEAR's protocol config at past blocks through the archival RPC (`fetch/protocol_history.py`), which dates each change to the day.
- **Scenarios.** The capture ratio is projected monthly from the last complete quarter. NEAR issued is supply × issuance rate ÷ twelve, under HSP-029's phase-in (the main path) and under today's rate. Intents revenue in NEAR starts at its trailing growth rate, measured from the data over the window set in `config.yaml`; the base case lets that growth halve every few years, the bull case holds it, the bear case has none. L1 burn is held at the last quarter's level and scaled up from the day all gas is burned. Inputs are in `config.yaml`.
- **Cross-checks** (`data/derived/crosschecks_monthly.csv`). {crosschecks}

### B. What we couldn't compute

- **NEAR AI Cloud's revenue and total usage.** Its usage and billing APIs need an organisation key, and NEAR AI publishes neither figure. We see OpenRouter traffic and on-chain staking only, and the OpenRouter revenue figure is an estimate at list prices.
- **Intents users and concentration across all channels.** The Explorer API covers the 1Click channel, about {oneclick_share} of Intents volume in {c3_month}. Swaps through other channels are in the volume figures (revenue.near.org, DefiLlama) but not in the user counts.
- **Confidential swaps.** The Explorer masks them, so they are missing from the user, referrer and chain breakdowns.
- **The whole cross-chain market.** DefiLlama's per-bridge volumes (Relay, deBridge, Across, Mayan and others) are paid-only, so C4's denominator is a peer set, not the whole market.
- **Gas paid by Intents transactions.** We count transactions to `intents.near`. Attributing gas needs receipt-level tables too large for our query budget.
- **Where all captured NEAR went.** {untraced} NEAR captured as Intents revenue is not in the three revenue wallets we track, and we couldn't trace it.
- **Whether AI credits get used.** Credit consumption happens off-chain.
- **A price target.** We don't model one. The thesis is about where value is created and how much of it reaches the token, and there is no reliable multiple for a token whose revenue mostly funds buybacks.

### F. Reproduce

1. `make setup` creates `.venv` and installs the pinned dependencies.
2. `make charts` rebuilds `data/derived/`, every chart, this document and the dashboard (`DASHBOARD.md`, and `site/index.html` with hover readouts and tables) from the committed data in a few seconds, with no keys.
3. `make verify` picks random past days, months and blocks from the committed data, fetches the same points from each live source and prints both values side by side, in about a minute with no keys. BigQuery's supply figures are checked against the archival RPC. Recent monthly Intents revenue on revenue.near.org is still settling for about three months after each month ends, so a change there is shown as "revised" rather than as a failure. The Explorer check needs the partner key and is skipped without it.

Refreshing the data is optional: `make fetch` (quick sources, no keys), `make fetch-bigquery` (needs a Google Cloud project), `make fetch-explorer` (needs a NEAR Intents partner JWT; slow because of the API's rate limit), `python -m fetch.protocol_history` (slow: the public archival node is rate-limited).

### G. Tools used

Python with requests, pandas, pyarrow, PyYAML and google-cloud-bigquery (pinned in `requirements.txt`). Charts are plain SVG drawn by `viz/svg.py`, with no plotting library; the dashboard's hover layer is `site/app.js`. Code and drafts were written with Claude Code (AI) and reviewed by the author. NEAR agent skills from `near/agent-skills`.
